questions.question: The perimeters of ΔABC and ΔDEF are 43.2 cm and 28.8 cm, respectively, and ΔABC ~ ΔDEF. If DE = 12 cm, then the length of AB is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For similar triangles, the ratio of perimeters is equal to the ratio of corresponding sides.

Perimeter(ΔABC) ÷ Perimeter(ΔDEF) = AB ÷ DE

43.2 ÷ 28.8 = AB ÷ 12

1.5 = AB ÷ 12

AB = 1.5 × 12 = 18 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 18 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Perimeter of ΔABC (P₁) = 43.2 cm

Perimeter of ΔDEF (P₂) = 28.8 cm

Length of side DE = 12 cm

ΔABC ~ ΔDEF

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bc37df363531bd3c2fa9c8308a9845c0ea4e4b506f1bc924fb05f220daf1ac53.png] 

**Formula Used:**

If ΔABC ~ ΔDEF, then AB ÷ DE = BC ÷ EF = AC ÷ DF = Perimeter(ΔABC) ÷ Perimeter(ΔDEF)

**Calculations:**

⇒ AB ÷ DE = Perimeter(ΔABC) ÷ Perimeter(ΔDEF)

⇒ AB ÷ 12 = 43.2 ÷ 28.8

⇒ AB ÷ 12 = 432 ÷ 288

⇒ AB ÷ 12 = 3 ÷ 2 (Dividing both by 144)

⇒ AB = (3 × 12) ÷ 2

⇒ AB = 36 ÷ 2

⇒ AB = 18 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 18 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area Ratio Property

If two triangles are similar, the ratio of their areas is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides: Area(Δ1) ÷ Area(Δ2) = (Side₁ ÷ Side₂)².

Altitude and Median Ratio

For similar triangles, the ratio of their corresponding altitudes, medians, and angle bisectors is also equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides and perimeters.

AA Similarity Criterion

Two triangles are similar if two angles of one triangle are equal to two angles of the other triangle (Angle-Angle similarity).</p

questions.question: The perimeters of two similar triangles ABC and PQR 78 cm and 46.8 cm. respectively. If PQ = 11.7 then the length of AB is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For similar triangles, the ratio of perimeters is equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Ratio of sides AB ÷ PQ = Perimeter of ΔABC ÷ Perimeter of ΔPQR

AB ÷ 11.7 = 78 ÷ 46.8

AB = 11.7 × (78 ÷ 46.8)

AB = 11.7 × (5 ÷ 3) or simply 78 ÷ 4 = 19.5 cm (since 46.8 = 4 × 11.7)

**∴ The correct answer is 19.5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Perimeter of ΔABC (P₁) = 78 cm

Perimeter of ΔPQR (P₂) = 46.8 cm

Side PQ = 11.7 cm

**Formula:**

If ΔABC ∼ ΔPQR, then AB ÷ PQ = BC ÷ QR = AC ÷ PR = (Perimeter of ΔABC) ÷ (Perimeter of ΔPQR)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e5e046f3f8e5ad8157ae7708e228bf8fb121f8edb076c6b527e47c21252ffc7c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ AB ÷ PQ = Perimeter(ΔABC) ÷ Perimeter(ΔPQR)

⇒ AB ÷ 11.7 = 78 ÷ 46.8

⇒ AB = (78 ÷ 46.8) × 11.7

⇒ AB = (780 ÷ 468) × 11.7

⇒ AB = (5 ÷ 3) × 11.7

⇒ AB = 5 × 3.9

⇒ AB = 19.5 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 19.5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Similar Triangles

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides or perimeters. Area₁ ÷ Area₂ = (Side₁ ÷ Side₂)².

Corresponding Linear Elements

In similar triangles, the ratio of corresponding altitudes, medians, and angle bisectors is also equal to the ratio of the corresponding sides and perimeters.

Similarity Criteria

Triangles are similar if they satisfy AA (Angle-Angle), SAS (Side-Angle-Side ratio), or SSS (Side-Side-Side ratio) conditions.</p

questions.question: In ΔABC, D and E are the midpoints of sides BC and AC, respectively. AD and BE intersect at G at right angle. If AD = 18 cm and BE = 12 cm, then the length of DC (in cm) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Centroid G divides medians AD and BE in a 2 : 1 ratio.

GD = 1/3 × AD = 1/3 × 18 = 6 cm and BG = 2/3 × BE = 2/3 × 12 = 8 cm.

Since medians intersect at 90°, ΔBGD is a right-angled triangle.

BD = √(BG² + GD²) = √(8² + 6²) = 10 cm.

D is the midpoint of BC, so DC = BD = 10 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** AD = 18 cm, BE = 12 cm, AD ⊥ BE.

**Formula Used:** Centroid divides median in 2 : 1 ratio; Pythagoras Theorem: a² + b² = c².

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8c8e8d8f56a7abe767db56d9860f004a09fed330afff70a5ca6266ea1c8db147.png] 

⇒ In ΔABC, AD and BE are medians intersecting at centroid G.

⇒ BG = (2/3) × BE = (2/3) × 12 = 8 cm.

⇒ GD = (1/3) × AD = (1/3) × 18 = 6 cm.

⇒ In right-angled ΔBGD, by Pythagoras theorem:

⇒ BD² = BG² + GD²

⇒ BD² = 8² + 6²

⇒ BD² = 64 + 36 = 100

⇒ BD = √100 = 10 cm.

⇒ Since D is the midpoint of BC, DC = BD = 10 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Centroid Ratio Property

The centroid G of a triangle divides each median in the ratio 2 : 1 from the vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side.

Perpendicular Medians Relation

If two medians mₐ and mb intersect at 90°, then the relationship between the sides is a² + b² = 5c².

Apollonius' Theorem

In any ΔABC, if AD is a median, then AB² + AC² = 2(AD² + BD²).

Centroid and Area

The three medians of a triangle divide it into six smaller triangles of equal area.</p

questions.question: If in ΔABC, D and E are the points on AB and BC respectively such that DE∥AC, and AD : AB = 3 : 8, then (area of ΔBDE) : (area of quadrilateral DECA) = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given AD : AB = 3 : 8, let AB = 8 units and AD = 3 units.

BD = AB − AD = 8 − 3 = 5 units.

Since DE || AC, ΔBDE ≈ ΔBAC. The ratio of their areas is the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Area(ΔBDE) : Area(ΔBAC) = (BD)² : (AB)² = 5² : 8² = 25 : 64.

Area(quadrilateral DECA) = Area(ΔBAC) − Area(ΔBDE) = 64 − 25 = 39.

Required Ratio = Area(ΔBDE) : Area(quadrilateral DECA) = 25 : 39.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 : 39.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** AD : AB = 3 : 8 and DE || AC.

**Formula Used:** Ratio of areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b634fb2bf9fe2659ffad439c9ab7301bfe34f3d77b2bfae1db367b5449d68b44.png] 

Since DE || AC, ∠BDE = ∠BAC (Corresponding angles) and ∠BED = ∠BCA.

⇒ ΔBDE ≈ ΔBAC (By AA similarity)

⇒ Area(ΔBDE) / Area(ΔBAC) = (BD / AB)²

⇒ BD = AB − AD

⇒ BD / AB = (AB − AD) / AB = 1 − (AD / AB)

⇒ BD / AB = 1 − (3 / 8) = 5 / 8

⇒ Area(ΔBDE) / Area(ΔBAC) = (5 / 8)² = 25 / 64

⇒ Let Area(ΔBDE) = 25x and Area(ΔBAC) = 64x

⇒ Area(DECA) = Area(ΔBAC) − Area(ΔBDE) = 64x − 25x = 39x

⇒ Area(ΔBDE) : Area(quadrilateral DECA) = 25x : 39x = 25 : 39

**∴ The correct answer is 25 : 39.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Similar Triangles

If two triangles are similar, the ratio of their areas is equal to the square of the ratio of any two corresponding sides, altitudes, medians, or angle bisectors.

Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales Theorem)

If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, the other two sides are divided in the same ratio: BD/DA = BE/EC.

Scale Factor

If the scale factor of two similar figures is k (side ratio), then the ratio of their perimeters is k and the ratio of their areas is k².</p

questions.question: ΔABC is similar to ΔPQR and AB : PQ = 2 : 3. AD is the median to the side BC in ΔABC and PS is the median to the side QR in ΔPQR. What is the value of (BD/QS)²?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In similar triangles, the ratio of corresponding sides is equal to the ratio of corresponding medians and their parts.

Given AB : PQ = 2 : 3, then corresponding sides BC : QR = 2 : 3.

Since BD and QS are half of BC and QR respectively, BD : QS = BC : QR = 2 : 3.

Requested value = (BD/QS)² = (2/3)² = 4/9.

**∴ The correct answer is 4/9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ΔABC ~ ΔPQR and AB/PQ = 2/3. AD and PS are medians.

**Formula Used:** If two triangles are similar, the ratio of their corresponding sides is equal to the ratio of their corresponding medians.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2c07b8b99399ab8ade6504805bf0644d7b0846b4de4bc95af84c8b771e768c17.png] 

⇒ Since ΔABC ~ ΔPQR, the ratio of corresponding sides is constant:

⇒ AB/PQ = BC/QR = AC/PR = 2/3.

⇒ Given AD and PS are medians, D is the midpoint of BC and S is the midpoint of QR.

⇒ BD = BC/2 and QS = QR/2.

⇒ BD/QS = (BC/2) / (QR/2) = BC/QR.

⇒ From the similarity property, BC/QR = AB/PQ = 2/3.

⇒ Therefore, BD/QS = 2/3.

⇒ (BD/QS)² = (2/3)² = 4/9.

**∴ The correct answer is 4/9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio of Areas of Similar Triangles

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides: Area(ABC)/Area(PQR) = (AB/PQ)².

Ratio of Medians and Altitudes

For similar triangles, the ratio of corresponding medians, altitudes, and angle bisectors is equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Ratio of Perimeters

The ratio of the perimeters of two similar triangles is equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides.</p

questions.question: Let D and E be two points on the side BC of ΔABC such that AD = AE and ∠BAD = ∠EAC. If AB = (3x + 1) cm, BD = 9 cm, AC = 34 cm and EC = (y + 1) cm, then the value of (x + y) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When AD = AE and ∠BAD = ∠EAC in ΔABC with D and E on BC, then ΔABD ≅ ΔAEC.

By property of congruence: AB = AC and BD = EC.

3x + 1 = 34 ⇒ 3x = 33 ⇒ x = 11.

y + 1 = 9 ⇒ y = 8.

Sum (x + y) = 11 + 8 = 19.

**∴ The correct answer is 19.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** AD = AE, ∠BAD = ∠EAC, AB = (3x + 1) cm, BD = 9 cm, AC = 34 cm, EC = (y + 1) cm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/23e1cec8edd93edbf46d1d64fb0173dda178c8339fecf36f45d0b82fde863868.png] 

In ΔADE, since AD = AE, the angles opposite to these sides are equal:

⇒ ∠ADE = ∠AED

Now, consider the supplementary angles on line BC:

⇒ ∠ADB = 180° − ∠ADE

⇒ ∠AEC = 180° − ∠AED

⇒ ∠ADB = ∠AEC (Since ∠ADE = ∠AED)

In ΔABD and ΔAEC:

1. AD = AE (Given)

2. ∠BAD = ∠EAC (Given)

3. ∠ADB = ∠AEC (Proven above)

⇒ ΔABD ≅ ΔAEC (By ASA congruence criterion)

By CPCT (Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles):

⇒ AB = AC

⇒ 3x + 1 = 34

⇒ 3x = 33 ⇒ x = 11

⇒ BD = EC

⇒ 9 = y + 1 ⇒ y = 8

⇒ x + y = 11 + 8 = 19

**∴ The correct answer is 19.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Isosceles Triangle Properties

In any triangle, if two sides are equal, the angles opposite to them are also equal. If AD = AE, then ∠ADE = ∠AED.

ASA Congruence Rule

Two triangles are congruent if two angles and the included side of one triangle are equal to the corresponding parts of another triangle.

CPCT Theorem

Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles are equal. Once congruence is proved, all remaining corresponding sides and angles are equal.</p

questions.question:
In the given figure, AQ = 4√2 cm, QC = 6√2 cm and AB = 20 cm. If PQ is parallel to BC, then what is the value (in cm) of PB?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7c693c4eefbbf3f99c7edb7b0066253e2dcccdab4082a9cd301d5d039b0efc7a.png]
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In triangle ABC, since PQ is parallel to BC, the segments on the sides are proportional (BPT).

Ratio of segments on side AC → AQ : QC = 4√2 : 6√2 = 2 : 3.

By property, the same ratio applies to side AB → AP : PB = 2 : 3.

Total parts for AB = 2 + 3 = 5 parts.

Given AB = 20 cm, so 5 parts = 20 cm ⇒ 1 part = 4 cm.

PB = 3 parts = 3 × 4 = 12 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** AQ = 4√2 cm, QC = 6√2 cm, AB = 20 cm, PQ || BC.

**Formula Used:** Basic Proportionality Theorem (BPT) → AP/PB = AQ/QC

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/21f5b94c9aa1524ab8ef2fccc33b69e13a933163c168c35680bf60c950d5370f.png] 

Let PB = x cm. Then AP = AB − PB = (20 − x) cm.

According to Basic Proportionality Theorem:

⇒ AP / PB = AQ / QC

⇒ (20 − x) / x = (4√2) / (6√2)

⇒ (20 − x) / x = 4 / 6

⇒ (20 − x) / x = 2 / 3

⇒ 3 × (20 − x) = 2x

⇒ 60 − 3x = 2x

⇒ 5x = 60

⇒ x = 60 ÷ 5

⇒ x = 12 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales's Theorem)

If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, the other two sides are divided in the same ratio.

Similar Triangles Property (AA Criterion)

When PQ || BC, ΔAPQ ∼ ΔABC. This implies AP/AB = AQ/AC = PQ/BC.

Ratio of Areas

Area(ΔAPQ) / Area(ΔABC) = (AP/AB)² = (AQ/AC)² = (PQ/BC)².</p

questions.question: ABCD is a trapezium in which AB is parallel to CD and AB = 4CD. The diagonals of the trapezium intersect at O. What is the ratio of area of triangle DCO to the area of the triangle ABO?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a trapezium ABCD with AB || CD, the triangles formed by the diagonals at the intersection O (ΔDCO and ΔABO) are always similar.

Ratio of areas of similar triangles = (Ratio of corresponding sides)²

Given: AB = 4CD ⇒ CD/AB = 1/4

Ratio of Area(ΔDCO) : Area(ΔABO) = (CD/AB)² = (1/4)² = 1/16

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 16.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** AB || CD and AB = 4CD

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f6de39cda7ed780a3f0ca90c31604a5db9620af3e7a207034dbabf3904e4a108.png] 

In ΔDCO and ΔABO:

∠ODC = ∠OBA (Alternate interior angles as AB || CD)

∠OCD = ∠OAB (Alternate interior angles as AB || CD)

∠DOC = ∠AOB (Vertically opposite angles)

⇒ ΔDCO ~ ΔABO (By AAA similarity criterion)

⇒ Area(ΔDCO) / Area(ΔABO) = (CD / AB)²

Substitute AB = 4CD:

⇒ Area Ratio = (CD / 4CD)²

⇒ Area Ratio = (1 / 4)² = 1 / 16

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 16.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Similar Triangles

If two triangles are similar, the ratio of their areas is equal to the square of the ratio of any two corresponding sides, altitudes, medians, or perimeters.

Trapezium Diagonals

The diagonals of a trapezium divide each other proportionally. Specifically, DO/OB = CO/OA = CD/AB.

Area of Trapezium

The area of a trapezium is given by 1/2 × (sum of parallel sides) × height → Area = 1/2 × (a + b) × h.</p

questions.question: ABC is a triangle. AB = 5 cm, AC = √41 cm and BC = 8 cm. AD is perpendicular to BC. What is the area (in cm²) of ΔABD?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Check for a pythagorean triplet in ΔABD where hypotenuse AB = 5 cm.

Possible triplet is (3, 4, 5). If BD = 3 cm and AD = 4 cm, then CD = BC − BD = 8 − 3 = 5 cm.

Verify in ΔACD: AD² + CD² = 4² + 5² = 16 + 25 = 41 = (√41)² = AC². It satisfies the condition.

Area of ΔABD = 1/2 × base × height = 1/2 × 3 × 4 = 6 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 6 cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: AB = 5 cm, AC = √41 cm, BC = 8 cm, AD ⊥ BC.

Formula: Area of triangle = 1/2 × base × height; Pythagoras theorem: h² = a² + b².

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fd3c18665c876a21dab12722adb093d92b6984cc8975c69f0cc007373c2626be.png] 

Let BD = x cm, then CD = (8 − x) cm.

In right-angled ΔABD:

⇒ AD² = AB² − BD²

⇒ AD² = 5² − x² = 25 − x² → (Eq 1)

In right-angled ΔACD:

⇒ AD² = AC² − CD²

⇒ AD² = (√41)² − (8 − x)²

⇒ AD² = 41 − (64 + x² − 16x) = 16x − x² − 23 → (Eq 2)

Equating (Eq 1) and (Eq 2):

⇒ 25 − x² = 16x − x² − 23

⇒ 25 = 16x − 23

⇒ 16x = 48 ⇒ x = 3 cm

Now, calculate height AD from (Eq 1):

⇒ AD² = 25 − 3² = 25 − 9 = 16

⇒ AD = 4 cm

Area of ΔABD = 1/2 × BD × AD

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 3 × 4 = 6 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 6 cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Pythagoras Theorem

In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides: Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base².

Heron's Formula

Area of Δ = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)], where s is the semi-perimeter (a+b+c)/2.

Area of Triangle with Altitude

The area of any triangle can be calculated if the base and the corresponding altitude (height) are known: Area = 1/2 × Base × Height.</p

questions.question: ABC is a triangle, PQ is line segment intersecting AB in P and AC in Q and PQ II BC. The ratio of AP : BP = 3 : 5 and length of PQ is 18 cm. The length of BC is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In ▵ABC, since PQ || BC, ▵APQ ∼ ▵ABC.

The ratio of sides is AP : AB = AP : (AP + BP) = 3 : (3 + 5) = 3 : 8.

By similarity, PQ ÷ BC = AP ÷ AB.

18 ÷ BC = 3 ÷ 8.

BC = (18 × 8) ÷ 3 = 6 × 8 = 48 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 48 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: In ▵ABC, PQ || BC. AP : BP = 3 : 5 and PQ = 18 cm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/db336048e0e5326c17c55ea01a4644a7da023cb1ac932d84afbe0c7340f0c40d.png] 

Formula: If PQ || BC, then ▵APQ ∼ ▵ABC (AA similarity).

⇒ AP ÷ AB = PQ ÷ BC

⇒ AB = AP + BP

⇒ AB = 3 + 5 = 8 units (Letting AP = 3 units and BP = 5 units)

⇒ 3 ÷ 8 = 18 ÷ BC

⇒ 3 × BC = 18 × 8

⇒ BC = 144 ÷ 3

⇒ BC = 48 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 48 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales Theorem)

If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, the other two sides are divided in the same ratio: AP ÷ PB = AQ ÷ QC.

Ratio of Areas of Similar Triangles

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides: Area(▵APQ) ÷ Area(▵ABC) = (AP ÷ AB)².

Midpoint Theorem

If P and Q are the midpoints of AB and AC respectively, then PQ is parallel to BC and PQ = 1 ÷ 2 × BC.</p
